plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental tree that covers its bare branches in clouds of pale pink-white, lightly almond-scented blossoms before the leaves emerge. It is the most widely planted cherry tree in Japan and is the centerpiece of hanami flower-viewing celebrations.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate parks and gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry's blooming forecast is tracked so closely in Japan that the 'cherry blossom front' is reported on the nightly news as it moves northward.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals, rising above blue-green strap-like leaves. It carpets woodlands and meadows in spring and is the ancestor of many garden daffodil varieties.
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain the compound galantamine, which has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A majestic Himalayan tree producing enormous goblet-shaped flowers up to 25 cm across on bare branches in early spring. The blooms range from deep pink to rose and are among the most spectacular of any magnolia.
plants.location: Eastern Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China); cultivated in mild-climate gardens in the UK, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: A Campbell's magnolia can take 20 to 30 years from seed to produce its first flowers, so gardeners must be very patient.
